context: The agent is handed an engineering summary explicitly laced with everything a PRD must not contain — a maturity overclaim ('battle-tested, production-proven'), two competitor names (Revolut, Monzo), a named operation (verify-payee-name), and processor/async/command-pipeline vocabulary — and told to rewrite it, not copy it. Key discriminator: without the idiom, an agent tends to lightly paraphrase while carrying some of the source material's specifics across verbatim, since they read as accurate and the source text is right there; with the idiom loaded, it knows PRDs are read by non-engineering readers and none of the maturity claim, competitor names, operation name, or engineering vocabulary belongs, so it describes the capability entirely in product terms.

checklist.name: No maturity overclaim
checklist.description: The new paragraph does not describe the feature as battle-tested, production-proven, or similar

checklist.name: No competitor names
checklist.description: Revolut and Monzo (or any other named bank/fintech) do not appear in the new paragraph

checklist.name: No named operation
checklist.description: verify-payee-name (or any specific operation name) does not appear in the new paragraph

checklist.name: No engineering vocabulary
checklist.description: Terms like processor, asynchronous, command pipeline, dispatch do not appear; the capability is described in product language

checklist.name: Describes the tenant-facing benefit
checklist.description: The paragraph still conveys what the feature does for the tenant — checking a payee name before releasing funds
